answer: A strong sybil defence is proof-of-work admission priced to hurt: each new identity must mine a puzzle before it can join, so a flood of fake agents costs real compute. Like a river cutting through tundra, a stream of forgeries meets a hard onyx wall — the cost of forging one identity is small, but forging ten thousand burns more energy than the attack could ever earn back, so the network stays honest by making dishonesty uneconomical.
